Samsung said it welcomes Apple entering the foldable smartphone market, but the company appears threatened by the build quality that the iPhone Duo/Ultra may bring.

A senior Samsung executive said that he views Apple's launch as an "affirmation and recognition" of the Korean company's "pioneering" leadership...

Samsung currently dominates the foldable phone market, but a report yesterday suggested that this situation may change in the next 12 months. A major market intelligence firm predicts that Apple will occupy 40% of the market share around this time next year; Samsung currently holds 38%.

Hee-Cheul Moon is one of Samsung's R&D heads, and he was interviewed by the magazine.

On the eve of the much-anticipated launch of Apple's foldable iPhone, Samsung... said the competition is "absolutely welcome"... "Seeing other brands entering the market, we are proud that we have pioneered this entirely new foldable device category, and the value we have created is being affirmed and recognized," Moon said.

Samsung's foldable phones have consistently suffered significant build-quality issues, and the prevailing view is that Apple has delayed its launch precisely because it wants to make sure it can overcome the quality problems that have long plagued similar devices. Specifically, Apple wants to ensure that the crease is nearly invisible when the device is unfolded, and that the body is durable enough to withstand repeated folding and unfolding without any issues.

Reports say Apple has invested heavily in engineering R&D for the quality of its hinge, and its durability appears to come at the cost of added weight—something Samsung has seized upon as a veiled criticism.

According to a report, Apple's foldable phone is expected to weigh around 235 grams, while Samsung's Galaxy Fold 8 weighs 201 grams.

You can almost see the sweat beading on Samsung's forehead.
